Kind: captions Language: en Hi everyone. I hope you're having a great day. Hope there was lots of sunshine and lots of fun. And I have another book. This one is called What Do You See When You Look at a Tree? What do you see when you look at a tree? What do you see when you look at a tree? leaves and twigs and branches or do you see a living thing that moves and breathes and dances? Pause and notice the trees all around you. Look closer and you'll see so much more. Trees are all different, special, unique. Just like the trees long before. Is this tree here like any other? Do any of these trees look the same? This is a Scots pine. This is a queen palm. This is a curly oak. And this is a mug pine. Most trees have branches, leaves, and a trunk, but each has its own special name. Does it lean on its friends? Does it swoop down low? Does it have branches perfect for climbing? Or does it stand proud on a far away hill waiting for the sun to start shining? Come a little nearer. What do you see? Is there an egg in a nest? Do squirrels dance rings around its great trunk? Can you see the robin's red breast? Let's take a peek under the roots. Can you see babies curled up with their mothers? Did you know that trees have families, too? They can speak to their sisters and brothers. Does this tree think? Does this tree feel? Does it have thoughts just like yours? Does it feel joy when the sun shines bright? Is it sad when the rain splatters and pours? What has a tree seen over hundreds of years? Who else has made a home in its arms? Did children before you play in its shade? Did they rub at its bark with their palms? What about the trees that are yet to be born, sleeping safely under the grasses? What will become of those new little plants? Who will love them with each year that passes? When they grow up, what might they become? Will their cherries be picked in the spring? Or maybe their wood be will be carefully carved into violins fitted with strings? Have you ever curled up with a tree in your hands as stories or songs in a book? Have you read till the moon and the stars filled the sky as you sat in a cozy old nook? And when you are bigger, where will you go? What new places will you explore? Will you go on adventures to faraway lands and gather stories from shore to shore? And when you're grown up, when time has passed and you've traveled the ocean blue, will you return to that very same tree that gave so much to you? Listening to trees. Slow down. Take a deep breath and look around. What can you see? What can you hear? Branches creek and leaves rustle. But did you know that trees can talk to each other? Science tells us that trees are far from silent. In fact, they are secretly speaking to one another all the time, right beneath our feet. So, trees can speak? Well, yes, but not with words. A network of fungi that grows around trees roots allows them to share nutrients and information with one another. This fungal network is called the woodwide web and it can stretch for hundreds of miles. Trees might exchange warnings about diseases or insects that pose a threat. They can also share food with one another and in some cases healthy trees can support trees that are sick or dying. Trees have families, too. When trees intertwine their root systems, they create family networks that can help and support one another. The biggest, oldest trees in the forest are called mothers. And just like human mothers, they take care of their offspring to give them a better chance of survival. Through this woodwide web, mother trees provide saplings with extra nutrients. They also use their large roots to carve out space for saplings to grow. Trees can even store memories to share with future generations. How to be more like a tree. There is so much we can learn from trees. They are a reminder to take our time, look out for one another, and look out for ourselves. too. Here are some different ways that we can be more treeish. Take your time. Trees can take hundreds of years to mature, growing little by little each day. They live long lives and see many things. Trees remind us that we need to be patient in order to grow strong. Self-care. Trees cannot survive without sunlight. Scientists think sunshine is vital to human happiness, too. When we feel positive and calm, our brains release a chemical called serotonin. Studies have shown that our brains release more serotonin when we are outside in the sunlight. Rest. In wintertime, many trees become dormant, a bit like how animals hibernate. They do this to protect themselves from the cold and ready themselves for spring. Trees remind us that it's important to make time for rest and relaxation. Be authentic. No two trees are the same, just as no two humans are exactly alike. Every tree twists and bends in its own way. Trees can teach us to be proud of our uniqueness and stand tall. Celebrate what makes you you. unlikely friendships. In a forest, every tree is valuable. If trees only looked after themselves, they wouldn't reach old age. That's why healthy trees support sick trees and young trees learn from older trees. We can do this in our everyday lives by working as a community. Spread your roots. Tree roots are buried deep beneath the soil and spread out over huge areas. This helps the tree to stay grounded while also allowing it to find new nutrients so that it can continue to grow. We can spread our own roots and grow by exploring the world around us. It's just as important to stay centered by surrounding ourselves with people who know and love us.

column5: 'The Three Billy Goats Gruff' read by Gary Oldman
column6:
'The Three Billy Goats Gruff' is written by Mac Barnett, illustrated by Jon Klassen and read by Gary Oldman.

A brilliantly crafted, hilarious twist on this beloved classic, 'The Three Billy Goats Gruff.'

Once there was a bridge and a terrible and VERY hungry troll lived underneath it. When the three Billy Goats Gruff decide to clip-clop across the bridge to get to the grassy ridge, the troll is already imagining all the way to prepare a delicious goat dinner. But the troll underestimates those seemingly sweet but oh-so-savvy goats! 

Told with pitch perfect timing and pacing, hilarious detail, and Barnett's signature narrator voice, this is Billy Goats Gruff as never before. High-stakes page turns will have readers on the edge of their seats and giggling along as they join each goat and anticipate the arrival of the hungry and terrible troll living under the bridge.

column6:
'Calvin Can't Fly: The Story of a Bookworm Birdie' is written by Jennifer Berne, illustrated by Keith Bendis and read by Jonathan Pryce.

Calvin is one unusual starling! While his siblings and cousins learn to fly, this rare bird lets his imagination soar while reading about pirates, dinosaurs, and other fascinating things. The other birds call him "geeky beaky," but Calvin just ruffles his feathers and buries his beak in a book. Yet, when it comes time to migrate, poor Calvin suddenly realizes he can't fly! His sisters, brothers, and cousins carry him into the air. But on their way south, the winds blow hard, the trees bend, and the air starts to smell strange. It's a hurricane, and only Calvin can save the day—because he has read all about it!

column6:
'Carla's Glasses' is written by Debbie Herman, illustrated by Sheila Bailey and read by Nicola Coughlan.

Carla loves to be different. So when her teacher announces an upcoming vision screening, Carla hopes she’ll be the only kid in class to need glasses. To prepare for her new look, she starts wearing homemade funky frames to school each day.

Turns out that the only one who needs glasses is Buster. But unlike Carla, Buster does NOT like to be different. He likes to blend in.

When Carla concocts an ingenious plan to help Buster, it’s clear to see that the power of friendship – and Carla’s creativity – will save the day.

This long-awaited companion to the award-winning Carla’s Sandwich will be adored by kids with or without glasses.

column6:
‘The Rooster Who Would Not Be Quiet!’ is written by Carmen Agra Deedy, illustrated by Eugene Yelchin and read by Anna Sawai.

La Paz is a happy but noisy village. A little peace and quiet would make it just right. So the villagers elect the bossy Don Pepe as their mayor. Before long, singing of any kind is outlawed. Even the teakettle is afraid to whistle! But there is one noisy rooster who doesn't give two mangos about this mayor's silly rules. Instead, he does what roosters were born to do. He sings: "Kee-kee-ree-KEE!"

The silenced populace, invigorated by the rooster's bravery, ousts the tyrannical mayor and returns their city to its free and clamorous state.

Carmen Deedy's masterfully crafted allegory and Eugene Yelchin's bright, whimsical mixed-media paintings celebrate the spirit of freedom and the courage of those who are born to sing at any cost.

column6:
‘Getting to Know Ruben Plotnick’ is written by Roz Rosenbluth, illustrated by Maurie J. Manning and read by Zach Braff.

What do you get when you put together the coolest kid in class, an unpredictable live-in grandmother, and a caring but anxious grandson? Disaster?

No. You get to know Ruben Plotnick.

David is worried about how zany Ruben Plotnick will react when he meets Grandma Rosie, who often says and does unexpected things. Will Ruben make fun of her to their classmates? Will he imitate her whispery voice? What will he do if Grandma Rosie suddenly wants to dance?

This heartwarming story of senility and school-age embarrassment reveals the importance of looking beneath the surface to really get to know someone.

Down home is Granny’s house. Down home is where Lil Alan and his parents and sister will gather with great-grandparents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins. Down home is where Lil Alan will hear stories of the ancestors and visit the land that has meant so much to all of them. column6:
‘Too Much Glue’ is written by Jason Lefebvre, illustrated by Zac Retz and read by Nicole Byer.

Matty LOVES glue. At home with Dad, he makes glue glasses, glue mustaches, and glue bouncy balls. But at school, Matty’s art teacher worries and warns, “Too much glue never dries.”

In art class one day, Matty decides to make the most fantastic glue project ever, with a super-special ingredient – himself! Ignoring his teacher’s warnings, Matty belly-flops onto the glue-covered table, rolls all around in the sequins and glitter, and encounters an unexpected glitch – when he tries to get up, he boings right back into the slippery, sticky mess!

This calls for a dose of imagination and a little help from friends. They try a gigantic tow truck, some yarn lassoes, and dabbing Matty with everything in the nurse’s bag – but each wacky attempt only makes things worse! Finally Matty gets an idea from his hyperventilating teacher.

Will it work, or will Matty be a half-boy, half-art project stuck-to-a-table forever?

column6:
‘The Three Questions’ is written and illustrated by Jon J Muth and read by Meryl Streep.

What is the best time to do things? Who is the most important one? What is the right thing to do? Nikolai knows that he wants to be the best person he can be, but often he is unsure if he is doing the right thing. So he goes to ask Leo, the wise turtle. When he arrives, the turtle is struggling to dig in his garden, and Nikolai rushes to help him. As he finishes work, a violent storm rolls in. Nikolai runs for Leo's cottage, but on his way, he hears cries for help from an injured panda. Nikolai brings her in from the cold, and then rushes back outside to rescue her baby too.

With stunning watercolors and a text that resounds with universal truths, this award-winning artist has based his first original story on one by Leo Tolstoy, transforming it into a timeless fable for young readers.

'La nevera de Maddi' es escrito por Lois Brandt, ilustrado por Vin Vogel, y leído por Isabella Gomez.

Sofía y Maddi viven en el mismo barrio, juegan en el mismo parque y van a la misma escuela. Pero mientras que la nevera de la casa de Sofía está siempre llena, la de Maddi siempre está vacía, completamente vacía, con solo un cartón de leche.

—¿Por qué tu mamá no va al mercado? —pregunta Sofía.
—Porque no tenemos suficiente dinero.
—¿Y qué pasa si les da hambre?
—Tenemos un poco de pan —dijo Maddi—.

Por favor, no se lo digas a nadie.
Sofía le promete a Maddi que no dirá nada, pero se propone ayudar a su mejor amiga. Esconde comida para llevarle a Maddi en su mochila, y pronto descubre que, aunque el pescado y los huevos son buenos para los niños, no lo son para las mochilas. Sin embargo, a pesar de las buenas intenciones y esfuerzos de Sofía, la realidad es que la nevera de Maddi continúa vacía.

Sofía prometió no decir nada. ¿Qué puede hacer entonces?

column6:
'The Busy Life of Ernestine Buckmeister' is written by Linda Ravin Lodding, illustrated by Suzanne Beaky and read by Connie Britton.

Ernestine is in over her head. Monday through Sunday, Ernestine’s week is packed with after-school lessons—tuba, knitting, sculpting, water ballet, yoga, yodeling, and karate. Overwhelmed and exhausted, Ernestine decides to take matters into her own hands and heads off to the park with her Nanny where she builds a fort, watches the clouds, and plays all kinds of unstructured and imaginative games. But when a teacher calls Ernestine's mom to report that she has not shown up for yodeling, her parents search everywhere until at last they hear their daughter's laughter coming from the park. Ernestine tells her parents what a wonderful afternoon she's had, and explains her plight, asking, "I like my lessons, but can't I stop some of them?" This saga hilariously captures the dilemma of the modern-day over-scheduled child in riotous color and absurd extremes. A delightful heroine, Ernestine will be sure to put “play” back on everyone’s agenda, demonstrating that in today’s overscheduled world, everyone needs the joy of play and the simple wonders of childhood.

column5: Why Storyline Online® Inspires Kids to Read | Celebrity Read-Alouds
column6:
Why does Storyline Online® inspire millions of children to fall in love with reading?

In this mini documentary, hear from actors and Storyline Online readers Jaime Camil and June Squibb, Storyline Online Executive Producer Rochelle Rose, 2nd grade teacher Melody Hou, school psychologist and parent Jenna Lizarraga, and student Isabella Lizarraga as they share why reading aloud is so important for kids — and the lasting impact of storytelling and the children's literacy program Storyline Online®.

Produced by the nonprofit SAG-AFTRA Foundation, Storyline Online has reached hundreds of millions of children worldwide with free read-aloud videos of beloved children’s books read by celebrated actors. Each video includes a Teacher’s Guide, aligned with Common Core Standards, to support reading comprehension, vocabulary and student engagement.

Explore the full Storyline Online library of free read-alouds for kids at: https://storylineonline.net

Thanks to all of the supporters of Storyline Online who participated in this project, and to SAG-AFTRA voiceover artist Andia Winslow for lending her voice and support.

Trusted by parents, teachers, and librarians, Storyline Online brings the joy of reading to children anytime, anywhere.

Discover the full library at https://storylineonline.net

column5: Storyline Online promo featuring Terry Crews, Rosario Dawson, Jennifer Garner and more!
column6:
The SAG-AFTRA Foundation's award-winning children's literacy program Storyline Online has released a new promotional video featuring readers Nancy Cartwright, Terry Crews, Rosario Dawson, Jennifer Garner, Joel McHale, and Seth Meyers encouraging children, parents and educators to discover its popular children's literacy program which has received more than 900 million views worldwide since 2001.

Endorsed by the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), Storyline Online® features over 85 read-alouds in its digital library, and provides free educational activity guides for teachers in classrooms, as well as parents with school-age children at home, to offer additional learning resources and support.

To join the reading adventure, visit www.storylineonline.net.

column5: 5 Centimeters per Second
column6:
Told in three interconnected segments, Takaki tells the story of his life as cruel winters, cold technology, and finally, adult obligations and responsibility converge to test the delicate petals of love.
Director Makoto Shinkai

There is a question whispered at the start of our story:
How fast do cherry blossoms fall?

The answer: about five centimeters per second.

Just like the drifting petals, human hearts, too, can fall… softly, slowly, and sometimes apart.

This is the story of Takaki Tōno — a boy, a teenager, a man — whose life unfolds in three chapters.
A story of love, distance, and the gentle ache of time.

The Tale of the Princess Kaguya

Long ago, in a time when gods walked in whispers and the moon bathed the earth in silver light, a humble bamboo cutter discovered a miracle.
This miracle would grow into a legend — of beauty, love, sorrow, and fate.
This is the story of the girl from the moon… The Tale of the Princess Kaguya.

Kaguya is a beautiful young woman coveted by five nobles. To try to avoid marrying a stranger she doesn't love, she sends her suitors on seemingly impossible tasks. But she will have to face her fate and punishment for her choices.
DirectorIsao Takahata

column5: Sweet Porridge   Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm
column6:
Sweet Porridge   Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm

Sweet Porridge - Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm


There was a poor but good little girl who lived alone with her mother, and they no longer had anything to eat. So the child went into the forest, and there an aged woman met her who was aware of her sorrow, and presented her with a little pot, which when she said, „Cook, little pot, cook,“ would cook good, sweet porridge, and when she said, „Stop, little pot,“ it ceased to cook.

The girl took the pot home to her mother, and now they were freed from their poverty and hunger, and ate sweet porridge as often as they chose. Once on a time when the girl had gone out, her mother said, „Cook, little pot, cook.“ And it did cook and she ate till she was satisfied, and then she wanted the pot to stop cooking, but did not know the word.


So it went on cooking and the porridge rose over the edge, and still it cooked on until the kitchen and whole house were full, and then the next house, and then the whole street, just as if it wanted to satisfy the hunger of the whole world, and there was the greatest distress, but no one knew how to stop it.

At last when only one single house remained, the child came home and just said, „Stop, little pot,“ and it stopped and gave up cooking, and whosoever wished to return to the town had to eat his way back.

column5: Greek myths, Medusa
column6:
Medusa is one of the most haunting and fascinating figures in Greek mythology 🐍.
Her story is a mix of beauty, tragedy, and monstrous transformation.
🧬 Origins and Family
Medusa was one of the three Gorgon sisters—alongside Stheno and Euryale.
Unlike her immortal siblings, Medusa was mortal, which made her vulnerable to death.
She was the daughter of Phorcys and Ceto, primordial sea gods.
💔 The Curse of Athena
Medusa was originally a beautiful maiden, admired for her stunning hair.
According to myth, she was either boastful about her beauty or violated by Poseidon in Athena’s temple.
Enraged, Athena transformed her into a monster with snakes for hair and a gaze that turned people to stone.
⚔️ Perseus and the Slaying
The hero Perseus was sent on a quest to slay Medusa.
With help from Athena and Hermes, he used a bronze shield to view her reflection and avoid her deadly gaze.
He beheaded Medusa while she slept, and from her blood sprang Pegasus (the winged horse) and Chrysaor, her children by Poseidon.
🛡️ Legacy and Symbolism
Perseus gave Medusa’s head to Athena, who placed it on her shield (the Aegis) as a protective emblem.
Her image became a symbol of protection and was used on armor and buildings to ward off evil.
Medusa’s myth has been reinterpreted over time—some see her as a tragic victim, others as a symbol of feminine rage and power.

column5: Your Name is no exception
column6:
Your Name is Japanese anime which Directed by Makoto Shinkai, the animation studio behind the movie Your Name is responsible for some of the most beautiful animated films ever made.
And Your Name is no exception. The movie follows two teenagers who share a profound, magical connection despite never having met before.
Takki Takachi Bana, a teenage boy from Tokyo, and Mizuhami Amemiya, a teenage girl who lives with her grandmother and little sister in the countryside, find themselves inexplicably drawn to each other.
Their connection is so strong that they begin to feel emotions and sensations that they have never felt before.
And they soon discover that they are swapping bodies whenever they fall asleep.
At first, they try to make the best of the situation and enjoy the newfound experiences that come with being in someone else 's body.
However, as time goes on, they begin to feel the downsides of not being able to control their own bodies
and the emotional toll it takes on them and those around them.
They make a pact to meet in person for the first time and try to sort things out.
But when they do meet, things don't exactly go according to plan.
The boy finds the girl's body and takes it back to his home in Tokyo, intending to return it to her the next day.
However, the girl's little sister gets sick and the boy ends up taking care of her instead.
In the meantime, the girl's grandmother becomes suspicious of the boy's presence in the house and confronts him.
She threatens to call the police if he doesn't leave, so the boy is forced to escape.
He runs into a convenience store and bumps into a friend of his who invites him to go see a fireworks festival with some other friends.
The boy accepts and spends the night with his friends, drinking, partying and letting loose.
Meanwhile, the girl wakes up in her own body again and is relieved to be reunited with her little sister.
The next morning, she finds a mysterious blue umbrella on the ground, which turns out to be a memento from the boy.
She keeps the umbrella and returns to Tokyo to find the boy and give him back his body.
But when she gets there, she finds that he has disappeared.
All she has to show for her adventure is a blue umbrella and a handful of memories.
Your Name is a beautifully animated film with a touching story and memorable characters.
It's a must-watch for fans of romance and body swap movies.
So if you haven't seen it yet, I highly recommend checking it out.

column5: Grave of the Fireflies, (Summary inspiration)
column6:
Grave of the Fireflies.
It's no secret that Japan was one of the most heavily bombed countries during World War II.
And in 1945, near the end of the war, an American B29 Super Fortress made a low altitude pass over the Japanese city of Kobe.
Its target, a factory complex that produced 80 percent of Japan's munitions. But the plane's bombardier made a mistake.
He dropped his payload early, killing hundreds of innocent civilians.
Among the dead were two children, a brother and sister who had been playing near their home when the bombs fell.
Their story is this anime's only reason for existing, though it's been retold countless times before.
It follows Seita and his little sister, who wake up in the hospital with no memory of the attack.
They're eventually discharged and they set out to find their mother, who they believe is still alive.
But their journey is fraught with danger. Food and supplies are scarce and the siblings must brave the elements and the hostility of strangers just to stay alive.
Along the way, they meet a handful of quirky characters, including an old woman who takes them in and a group of children who befriend them.
But the adults in this world are mostly uncaring and the children are forced to fend for themselves.
The animation is gorgeous, but the story is painfully slow.
For the first 20 minutes, not a single word is spoken.
The film 's first few scenes are so effective that it 's hard to imagine how the story could possibly go anywhere from there.
So if you're expecting Grave of the Fireflies to be a sweeping epic, you'll probably be disappointed.
If, however, you're in the mood for a character study, this movie is perfect.
We get to see how far a young boy will go to protect his sister and how far a little girl will go to protect her brother.
Their relationship is the heart and soul of this movie.
And while it might not have the action and excitement of other wartime movies, it's all the better for it.
This is a quiet, character-driven drama that will stay with you long after the credits roll.

column5: Goldilocks and the Three Bears,
column6:
Goldilocks and the Three Bears,
Based on the Charming version by the Victorian writer Andrew Lang.

Once upon a time there were three bears, who lived together in a house of their own in a wood. One of them was a little, small wee bear; one was a middle-sized bear, and the other was a great, huge bear.

One day, after they had made porridge for their breakfast, they walked out into the wood while the porridge was cooling. And while they were walking, a little girl came into the house. This little girl had golden curls that tumbled down her back to her waist, and everyone called her by Goldilocks.

Goldilocks went inside. First she tasted the porridge of the great, huge bear, and that was far too hot for her. And then she tasted the porridge of the middle bear, and that was too cold for her. And then she went to the porridge of the little, small wee bear, and tasted that. And that was neither too hot nor too cold, but just right; and she liked it so well, that she ate it all up.

Then Goldilocks went upstairs into the bed chamber and first she lay down upon the bed of the great, huge bear, and then she lay down upon the bed of the middle bear and finally she lay down upon the bed of the little, small wee bear, and that was just right. So she covered herself up comfortably, and lay there until she fell fast asleep.

By this time, the three bears thought their porridge would be cool enough, so they came home to breakfast.

“SOMEBODY HAS BEEN AT MY PORRIDGE!” said the great huge bear, in his great huge voice.

“Somebody has been at my porridge!” said the middle bear, in his middle voice.

Then the little, small wee bear looked at his, and there was the spoon in the porridge pot, but the porridge was all gone.

“Somebody has been at my porridge, and has eaten it all up!” said the little, small wee bear, in his little, small wee voice.

Then the three bears went upstairs into their bedroom.

“SOMEBODY HAS BEEN LYING IN MY BED!” said the great, huge bear, in his great, rough, gruff voice.

“Somebody has been lying in my bed!” said the middle bear, in his middle voice.

And when the little, small, wee bear came to look at his bed, upon the pillow there was a pool of golden curls, and the angelic face of a little girl snoring away, fast asleep.

“Somebody has been lying in my bed, and here she is!” Said the little, small wee bear, in his little, small wee voice.

Goldilocks jumped off the bed and ran downstairs, out of the door and down the garden path. She ran and she ran until she reached the house of her grandmama. When she told her grandmama about the house of the three bears who lived in the wood, her granny said: “My my, what a wild imagination you have, child!”

column5: Rapunzel was a princess kidnapped by a witch
column6:
Rapunzel
Rapunzel was a princess kidnapped by a witch when she was a kid for her magical hair. Rapunzel did not know that she was kidnapped by the witch pretending to be her mother, and she wanted her for her magical hair. Every day the witch combed Rapunzel's long beautiful hair  so that by touching her hair, she could look younger than her real age. Witch every time, Witch lies to Rapunzel that the outside world is not good for her, and she should always sit in their castle for their safety.
Slowly, Rapunzel discovered the outside world with the help of a stranger she met at her castle and faced many obstacles in the outside world and discovered that the witch was not her birth mother; she kidnapped her. Rapunzel learnt that she had magical long hair, for which the witch wanted her. Ultimately, she bravely fought the witch and reunited with her birth parents.

column5: The Carpet That Would Not Fly
column6:
Once upon a time in a far away land, there was a Sultan's daughter who was renowned throughout the kingdom for her extraordinary beauty.
But the princess had a rather peculiar habit. Every night before she went to bed  she would take out a magic carpet that could fly and zoom around the palace  up and down the corridors
 over the fountains and gardens  and sometimes even outside the palace walls  which of course was quite dangerous since it was practically impossible to navigate the busy streets of the city at night.
But one day while flying over the marketplace, the princess saw a handsome young man named Hassan who was delivering bread to the shops.

column5: The Three Apples
column6:
In this story, an angler finds a chest in the Tigris River that he offers to Harun al-Rashid, the Abbasid Caliph. Harun finds that it contains the body of a dead lady and orders his counselor, Ja'far, to tackle it.
The dead lady's husband and father both claimed to have killed her, however, the Caliph accepts the tale of the spouse who trusted her to have been untrustworthy. The spouse had purchased three exceptional apples for her when she was sick, and when he found a slave with one of the apples, the slave guaranteed his sweetheart gave it to him. In a fury, the man killed his wife. The slave who created all the mischief turns out to be Ja'far's, and Ja'far asks for an exoneration.

column5: Mid Autumn Festival or the Moon Festival
column6:
The Mid Autumn Festival or the Moon Festival is a traditional Chinese holiday celebrated every year on the 15th day of the 8th month on the Chinese calendar.
This year it falls on September. It's a time for family reunions, just like Thanksgiving here in the States, but with a lunar twist.
The holiday is all about appreciating the beauty of the moon and giving thanks to the moon goddess Chang' e.
According to legend, Chang' e was an ordinary woman who was chosen to become the moon goddess after she accidentally drank an elixir that was meant for her husband, the Jade Emperor.
After she ascended to the moon, she was lonely and each year on this day, her husband would visit her and they would enjoy the reunion until, you know, he kicked her to the curb for good.
So, you know, the Jade Emperor, he's not really the nice guy you want to be stuck at home with.
Anyway, people celebrate the holiday by getting together with their families and eating mooncakes.
Mooncakes are delicious pastries filled with sweet or savory ingredients and they come in all shapes and sizes, just like the moon, which is said to be at its fullest and brightest on this night.
The round shape of the mooncakes symbolize the full moon and the reunion of families.
The most popular flavor is probably the lotus seed paste, but there's also bean, red bean, coconut, egg yolk, green tea and even durian.
You can also get really fancy ones like this five thousand dollar gold one that's actually edible. No joke.
Another fun thing about the holiday is the lantern riddles.
During the Lantern Festival, which takes place the day after the Moon Festival, people will set up elaborate lanterns
and then take turns trying to guess the riddles that are written on them.
Whoever guesses correctly gets to keep the lantern.
So if you're in China for this holiday, be sure to try some mooncakes and maybe even do a little lantern riddle guessing.
And if you can't be in China, then just stay up late and appreciate the moon from wherever you are.
Because even though we might be miles away from our loved ones, we can still come together and appreciate the beauty of the natural world.
Just don't stare too long at your phone. Put it down, look up and take in the view.
After all, that's what the moon goddess Chang'e would want us to do.
Thanks for watching and I'll see you next time.

column5: Tale of Two Witches
column6:
Once upon a time in a spooky old house on a dark and stormy night, there lived a kind witch named Hazel.
She brewed magical potions and cast delightful spells, spreading joy throughout the neighborhood.
But alas, her sister, the dreadful Griselda, practiced wicked witchcraft and longed to rule the town with an iron fist.
Now, despite their differences, they shared one thing in common, a deep love for cats.
And when a lost kitten meowed pitifully on their doorstep, Hazel took it in without hesitation.
But Griselda, with her heart as cold as a witch's cauldron, flung the poor creature out into the storm.
"A witch's house is no place for a stray," she cackled.
"Quick, get out of here before I turn you into a toad."
However, something remarkable happened.
Instead of cowering in fear, the kitten stood its ground, arched its back and let out a mighty roar that shook the very foundations of the house.
Startled by this unexpected display of bravery, Griselda retreated into her room, leaving Hazel to care for the kitten.
As the days passed, the kitten grew stronger and more courageous, and Hazel couldn't help but feel a sense of pride.
She named him Midnight and taught him how to fish for compliments with a magic wand and yarn ball.
Together, they explored the enchanting Whispering Woods, where trees gossiped secrets and flowers bloomed in every color imaginable.
Meanwhile, Griselda seethed with envy, watching from afar as Hazel and Midnight became the talk of the town.
"That wretched cat has brought nothing but chaos to my peaceful home," she grumbled.
"I must do something drastic before my cauldron bubbles over with rage."
And so the wicked witch concocted a wicked plan.
She transformed herself into a beautiful white dove and flew to the village, where she cast a spell on the baker, causing him to fall madly in love with the first person he laid eyes on, which, ugh, just happened to be Griselda.
Then she repeated the process with the cobbler, the tailor and every eligible bachelor in town until she had an entire army of lovestruck men at her command.
With their help, she marched on Hazel's house, determined to put an end to her sister's happiness once and for all.
But little did she know that Midnight had overheard her plans and had already alerted his fairy godmother, the great and powerful Luna.
As Griselda's goons approached the house, Luna swooped down from the sky, transforming Midnight into a magnificent lion with a flick of her magic wand.
Startled by the sudden appearance of a real life Disney character, the men froze in their tracks.
Then, with a deafening roar, the lion pounced, sending them running for their lives.
Griselda, however, was not so easily defeated. She raised her hands and unleashed a torrent of dark magic, but Luna was unfazed.
With a wave of her wand, she banished Griselda's spells and sent her tumbling into her own cauldron.
"It's over, Griselda," Luna boomed. "Your reign of terror ends today."
But before she could finish the job, a tiny meow interrupted her.
Startled, Luna turned and saw Hazel standing before her, holding a small, familiar looking kitten in her arms.
"Please, Great Luna," Hazel pleaded. "My sister may be misguided, but she's still my family.
I beg you, spare her life and turn her into a cat instead."
Touched by Hazel's compassion, Luna agreed. And with a wave of her magic wand, Griselda was transformed into a fluffy grey tabby cat.
As the townspeople looked on, Hazel and Griselda embraced, realizing that love and kindness were far more powerful than any curse or spell.
They lived happily ever after, or at least until next week's episode.

column5: Even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain
column6:
Even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain.
That's what this saying in Japanese means. And it's a great life lesson for us all to remember.
Imagine a young man who wants to be the strongest, most successful businessman in the world.
He sets this big goal for himself. And every day he thinks about how far he is from actually achieving that goal. He feels so little and so powerless.
So he just gives up and figures he'll never accomplish anything because he's not special.
Now imagine another man who also wants to be the strongest businessman in the world. But every day he just does a little bit of reading.
He learns one new thing and practices that one new thing for the rest of the day.
He does this for a week and then goes back to work the next week and applies what he learned that week.
And he does this consistently until one day he becomes the most successful businessman in the world.
It's the same exact goal, but why did only one of them achieve it?
It's because of this saying, Chiri mo tsumoreba yama to naru, even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain.
No matter how small your efforts are, if you do them consistently over a long period of time, they will add up and become significant.
We often think we need to do something big to change our lives, but that's just not true. We can change our lives with small consistent efforts.
The secret to success in anything is to break it down into smaller actions.
For example, if you want to be the best at basketball, you can break it down into smaller actions like shooting 10 free throws every day or running 1 mile every day.
Once you have these small goals, it's much easier to achieve them and you'll see progress much faster.
And here's the beautiful thing about this quote. It doesn't matter what you do, only that you do it consistently.
The type of action doesn't matter as much as the consistency of the action.
You could be watering other people's plants and it would still apply.
As long as you're consistent, your efforts will eventually turn into a mountain, even if that mountain isn't exactly what you had envisioned.
So my question for you is, what small effort can you do today that will make a big difference in your life tomorrow? What small habits can you start building?
And I want you to really think about this because it's a serious question.
If you can identify those small actions, then you're one step closer to changing your life.

It’s hedgehog‘s birthday and she’s very excited! She would like to ask all of her forest friends to help her celebrate. But everyone seems so busy. The squirrels are merrily decorating the trees, bear is sweeping up a storm, and bunny is gathering lots of delicious food. Every time hedgehog tries to speak, the words don’t seem to come out right! Can hedgehog be brave and invite her friends to help her celebrate her special day before it’s too late, or is she just too timid to talk?

column6:
Today’s The day little monkey is learning to climb by himself. He wants to play in the trees with his cousins, but he just can’t seem to figure it out. He slips, slides, gets tangled, and tumbles! As he and his mommy take a break to visit their friends in the jungle, they discover baby sloth learning to sleep safely, Little armadillo learning how to roll, and little flamingo trying to balance. Will little monkey learned from his friends and be able to join his family in the tree tops, or is he simply too clumsy to climb?

Welcome to Storytime with Lorenzo Our featured book Today Wednesday I am Wednesday illustrated by Vivien Wu Creatively Read and Adapted by Lorenzo Wednesday Hello, Dear Reader. I assume you are reading this book because you're a  little like me. My name is Wednesday Addams. I'm not like other kids.  (And anyone who messes with my little brother finds that out the hard way.) My father calls me his little storm cloud, which is fitting because... ... my mother adores dark rainy days and thunderstorms.   And my father adores my mother. It's gross. I was born on Friday the thirteenth, supposedly  a day of very bad luck. My mother named me Wednesday after a line in a famous poem: Wednesday's child is full of woe. I am now being sent to Nevermore Academy. Nevermore is a school for werewolves, vampires, gorgons,  sirens, and other kinds of outcasts. Whether or not I fit in as an outcast,  I know what I do like and what I don't like. And that makes some people uneasy, for some reason. For example, I like Thing. My parents sent him to keep an eye on me at school,  but I made him swear loyalty to me  instead. Now my five-fingered friend gives me a hand with whatever I get up to . . . . . whether it's playing music. .. ... or solving mysteries. And there are a lot of mysteries to  solve at Nevermore. My roommate, Enid, is different from me. She likes lots of color... and unicorns. Black is my color  and will do just fine for almost every situation. Enid is also a werewolf and a hugger. I like  werewolves well enough... .. but hugs not so much. (You can let go now.) I like fencing, the art of sword fighting.  It's a dangerous way to get good exercise. Today, Bianca is my opponent. She'll do anything to win, so I like to best her  whenever I can. But I have to admit, she's quite good with a sword. People say my moves are  strange, and that might be true-  but I'm Wednesday Addams, and I believe... Seeing as how we are about to part, Dear Reader, I will admit to  liking one last thing -dancing... when the music is to my liking. The End Thanks for reading with me. He knows when to fight ... . . . when to stay out of the way... . . . and when to comfort a friend in need. He can fit in small places, so he's helpful on secret missions . . . . . . and when pulling off pranks and surprises. Though sometimes  the surprise is for . . . . . . me! Happy birthday, Wednesday! Speaking of surprises, most people would never guess that Thing is an excellent swimmer. . . ... and the teammate the Black Cats needed to win the Poe Cup! Thing can be thoughtful. (He's not even the WEIRDEST member of the family. . . .) He may only be four fingers and a thumb, but you have to hand it to Thing . . . he's as clever, brave, and loyal as any disembodied hand could be. Welcome to story  time with Lorenzo. Our featured   book today is The Adams Family. Meet the family. Creatively Read and Adapted by Lorenzo This is the Addams Family.  They do things a little  differently from other people. Everyone seems to think that  they are terribly strange. People seem to be afraid of them! As you might think,  they don't get many visitors. They live in a mansion on a hill. The Addams Family is a bit  different from other people. They prefer tricks to treats. Don't even get them started on sunshine.  In fact, they think thunderstorms make the perfect weather. Uncle Fester is Gomez’s unusual brother. Grandma is Gomez’s even more unusual mother. Lurch is the butler. Thing also helps around the house. Not only do they act a little strange,   but they even have strange names! Gomez and Morticia are married. Their children are Wednesday and Pugsley. Sometimes the Addams Family does act  like other people. For example, they have a pet.  His name is Kitty. But Kitty is a lion!  No one wants to come over with a pet lion lying around! This is Gomez Addams. He's a sharp dresser.  Just look at his suit and tie! Not only is he a sharp dresser,  but he also has a sharp mind. When he gets an idea,  he gets very excited. Especially if the idea is terrible. This is Morticia Addams. Her style is like her husband's.  She adores her black dress because it looks great  against her gray skin! Morticia is the head  of the Addams Family household. She keeps the other heads in line,  whether they are big or small. Morticia and Gomez are crazy in love.  Their favorite thing to do together is dance. Morticia's favorite dance is a little dangerous.  She spins Gomez quickly across the floor. These lovebirds are surprisingly good at dancing.  No one would ever guess that Gomez has two left feet!  He keeps the two left feet in his closet. This is Wednesday Addams. At thirteen, she is the big sister  in the family. You will recognize Wednesday  by her braids and cold expression. Wednesday does things on her own.  She spends a lot of her time thinking of ways to trick people. Wednesday is highly intelligent. She always comes up  with amazing science experiments.  But her science experiments tend to be creepy. One time, she brought a dead frog back to life! Can you imagine a house full of zombie frogs? This is Pugsley Addams. He is ten and the only person  in his family with blond hair. Although he may not  look like his family, he is just as sinister. Pugsley loves anything that is extremely speedy. He builds his own toys. Pugsley is a bit of a mad scientist. Like his sister, Wednesday, He can create things like powerful rockets. Sometimes his inventions aren't very safe. But most of all, Pugsley loves  it when his experiments explode! He is the family butler. When he answers the door,  he doesn’t make the best first impression. His massive height and greenish skin  make visitors think he’s a monster - and sometimes people run away! But he is not as scary as he seems!  Lurch cares for the children. He's almost like their nanny! LGB Book 3 page 12 Lurch loves to play the piano.  He is surprisingly good! Thing loves Lurch's music too.  Even though Thing does not have ears, he always snaps along. This is Uncle Fester. He has no hair and wears a big, heavy coat.  He loves to sing.  But his shrill voice scares people away. This is Grandma. She is Gomez's mother.  She loves to go on adventures all around the world.  She has a reputation for being good at card playing.  Some people think she is a rotten cheater.  But they are wrong. She's actually a very good cheater. This is Thing. Thing is a hand.  No... really! Thing is left-handed.  He uses his fingers to walk around. He doesn't speak,  but he can show you what he's thinking. People think that  the Addams Family is a little scary. The truth is, they are truly terrifying!  Actually, the only thing that isn't so spooky  is how much they love each other. This is the Addams Family. The End Thanks for reading with me. Welcome to Storytime with Lorenzo, where reading is fun, spooky, and full of imagination! 📚✨

Today’s featured story is The Little Golden Book Version of
 “The Addams Family: Meet the Family”
Illustrated by Vivien Wu and creatively read and adapted by Lorenzo.
This is Book 3 of 3 in our Addams Family read-aloud series! 🖤

Meet Gomez, Morticia, Wednesday, Pugsley, Uncle Fester, Grandma, Lurch, and Thing — the wonderfully weird Addams Family who love thunderstorms, tricks, and all things spooky! ⚡🦇

Even though they seem strange, one thing’s for sure — they love each other dearly. ❤️

🎧 Watch the full story and discover:
Why Wednesday’s science experiments are a little creepy 🧪
What makes Pugsley’s inventions go boom! 💥
How Lurch and Thing make beautiful music together 🎹
Why being different can make your family truly special 👻

💬 Lesson of the Story:
Families come in all shapes and styles — and being different is what makes you unique!

column6: Kind: captions Language: en Hello Everyone! Welcome to Storytime with Lorenzo, Today’s featured book is  dedicated to all the little ones  who aspire to become athletes, and  to everyone who loves Basketball. Little People, BIG DREAMS Michael Jordan Written by: Maria Isabel Sanchez Vergara Illustrated by: Lo Harris Creatively Read and Adapted by Lorenzo. If your new to my channel, please subscribe and help my channel grow. Have you ever wanted to be the  best at something you love?  Let’s find out how little Michael Jordan  became one of the greatest  basketball players in history! Little Michael grew up in  a town in North Carolina. He was the fourth kid of the Jordans,  but he always wanted to be  the first at everything. Especially if that meant beating  his older brother, Larry. Hoping they would not just be  fierce competitors but good teammates, his parents encouraged their kids to play all kinds of sports. And Michael learned that talent may win a game, but only teamwork can win a championship. One day, Michael came home from school crying. He hadn't been selected for the basketball team because he was too short! His mother wiped his tears and told him what she used to say to all her kids: "Go out and earn it." Michael spent all summer practicing with the ball. When it was time to go back to class, he had not just gained self-confidence; he had grown taller, too. Soon, he was the star of the Buccaneers, his high school team. Whether it was defending the hoop, stealing balls,  or making impossible jumps,  he was the best on the court. Many colleges set their sights on him,  and Michael accepted a scholarship to the University of North Carolina. Michael went from scoring the winning shot at the  college finals to receiving  a gold medal at the Olympics. With "23" on his back,  he joined the Chicago Bulls at the NBA, the biggest professional league in the world. The Bulls had never landed a title. Still, Michael was there to do what teammates do: help each other become better players. Six years later, they won their first championship and they kept winning-three times in a row! When the best NBA stars were invited to participate at the Olympics,  Michael knew that the gold medal would come home with them. The whole world went wild watching the Dream Team,  the most incredible team ever assembled. Michael was so famous that even a pair of sneakers were named after him! But when his father died, he was heartbroken and quit basketball. He sought comfort playing baseball, his dad's favorite sport. It took him a year to realize  that his place was on the  basketball court, next to his teammates. Everyone who loved the game was happy to see Michael lead the Bulls  to win their fourth championship on a very special date: Father's Day. Air is Back Go Bulls! Thanks MJ We Love You! One day, his coach Phil announced that it was his last season with the team. Michael and his teammates wanted to make sure it ended right! And after winning his sixth title,  it was time for His Airness to hang up his sneakers, too. Whether he was playing with one of his five kids or raising money  to help other children, Michael never stopped competing. He became a successful businessman supporting  all kinds of sports: from golf to car racing. By expecting things of himself before he could even do them,  little Michael became the biggest legend in the history of basketball.  And an inspiration for others to choose their dream... and make it happen! Michael Jordan (Born 1963) Michael Jordan was born on February 17th, 1963, in Brooklyn, New York. One of five children, Michael's  family moved to Wilmington,  North Carolina, when he was very young. His father was a General  Electric plant supervisor,  and his mother worked at a bank. Michael loved sports, and his parents   encouraged him to try everything. He didn't make his high school   basketball team as a sophomore... but he trained hard and the following year,  he made the team! After high school, he won a basketball scholarship  to the University of North Carolina, where he played under head coach Dean Smith. In Michael's first season at North Carolina he was named Rookie of the Year for 1982.  He was selected by the Chicago Bulls of  the National Basketball Association (NBA)  as the third pick of the 1984 draft. He went on to play 1,072 NBA games, becoming known for his "airtime"-a 4-foot   vertical leap for the basket- taking the Bulls to six NBA   championships with his coach, Phil Jackson. He won Most Valuable Player four times, as well as two Olympic Gold medals  as part of America's most famous  national squad: the Dream Team. When he retired from basketball,  his determination never left him,  believing that "you have to expect things  of yourself before you can do them." He has gone on to run charities,  make movies, and work in business. In 2016, he was presented with the  Presidential Medal of Freedom by Barack Obama. Today, Michael is loved by  people all over the world,  and is considered by basketball fans as the greatest player to ever step onto the court. Lesson of the Story Michael Jordan's story shows us that  hard work and believing in yourself  can help you achieve your dreams. Even when he faced challenges, like  not making the basketball team,  he kept practicing and never gave up. This teaches us that teamwork is important too. When we help each other, we can do great things! Remember, if you work hard and stay positive, you can reach your goals just like Michael did! The End Please subscribe for more Fun and Exciting   Read Aloud Videos on Storytime with Lorenzo. Thanks For Watching! If you like this Video, Like and Subscribe!

column6: Kind: captions Language: en Hello everyone!  Welcome to Story Time with Lorenzo. These are Dr Suess compilation videos.  Stay tuned for fun segments  at the end of each book. 1. The Cat in the Hat Our Featured Book Today is ... The Cat in the Hat By Dr. Seuss Creatively Read and Adapted by Lorenzo What would you do if you were stuck inside on  a rainy day? Would you like a surprise visitor? The Cat in the Hat The sun did not shine. It was too wet to play.  So we sat in the house. All that cold, cold, wet day. I sat there with Sally. We sat there, we two.  And I said, "How I wish We had something to do!" Too wet to go out And too cold to play ball.  So we sat in the house. We did nothing at all. So all we could do was to  Sit! Sit!  Sit! And we did not like it. Not one little bit. And then Something went BUMP! How that bump made us jump! We looked! Then we saw him step in on the mat! We looked! And we saw him! The Cat in the Hat! And he said to us,  "Why do you sit there like that?" "I know it is wet And the sun is not sunny.  But we can have Lots of good fun that is funny!" "I know some good games we could play," Said the cat.  "I know some new tricks," Said the Cat in the Hat.  "A lot of good tricks. I will show them to you.  Your mother Will not mind at all if I do." Would you trust the Cat in the Hat to play  games in your house while your mom is away? Then Sally and I Did not know what to say.  Our mother was out of the house For the day. But our fish said, “No! No! Make that cat go away!  Tell that Cat in the Hat You do NOT want to play.  He should not be here. He should not be about.  He should not be here When your mother is out!" "Now! Now! Have no fear. Have no fear!" said the cat.  "My tricks are not bad," Said the Cat in the Hat.  "Why, we can have Lots of good fun, if you wish,  With a game that I call UP-UP-UP with a fish!" "Put me down!" said the fish.  "This is no fun at all! Put me down!" said the fish. "I do NOT wish to fall!" "Have no fear!" said the cat. "I will not let you fall.  I will hold you up high As I stand on a ball.  With a book on one hand! And a cup on my hat!  But that is not ALL I can do!" Said the cat . . . "Look at me! Look at me now!" said the cat.  "With a cup and a cake On the top of my hat!  I can hold up Two books! I can hold up the fish! And a little toy ship! And some milk on a dish! And look! I can hop up and down on the ball! But that is not all! Oh, no. That is not all... "Look at me! Look at me! Look at me NOW! It is fun to have fun But you have to know how. I can hold up the cup And the milk and the cake!  I can hold up these books! And the fish on a rake! I can hold the toy ship And a little toy man!  And look! With my tail I can hold a red fan! I can fan with the fan  As I hop on the ball! But that is not all. Oh, no. That is not all. . . .” That is what the cat said... Then he fell on his head! He came down with a bump From up there on the ball.  And Sally and I, We saw ALL the things fall! And our fish came down, too. He fell into a pot! He said, "Do I like this? Oh, no! I do not.  This is not a good game," Said our fish as he lit. Why is the fish not happy with the Cat in the Hat? "No, I do not like it, Not one little bit!" "Now look what you did!"  Said the fish to the cat. "Now look at this house! Look at this! Look at that! You sank our toy ship,  Sank it deep in the cake. You shook up our house  And you bent our new rake. You SHOULD NOT be here When our mother is not.  You get out of this house!" Said the fish in the pot. "But I like to be here.  Oh, I like it a lot!" Said the Cat in the Hat To the fish in the pot. "I will NOT go away. I do NOT wish to go! And so," said the Cat in the Hat, "So  So So . . . I will show you Another good game that I know!" And then he ran out. And, then, fast as a fox,  The Cat in the Hat Came back in with a box. A big red wood box. It was shut with a hook.  "Now look at this trick," Said the cat. "Take a look!" Then he got up on top With a tip of his hat. "I call this game FUN-IN-A-BOX," Said the cat. "In this box are two things I will show to you now.  You will like these two things," Said the cat with a bow. How would you feel if the Cat brought in some  mysterious friends? Are you ready to meet them? "I will pick up the hook. You will see something new.  Two things. And I call them Thing One and Thing Two.  These Things will not bite you. They want to have fun." Then, out of the box Came Thing Two and Thing One! And they ran to us fast. They said, "How do you do?  Would you like to shake hands With Thing One and Thing Two?" And Sally and I Did not know what to do.  So we had to shake hands With Thing One and Thing Two.  We shook their two hands. But our fish said, "No! No!  Those Things should not be In this house! Make them go! "They should not be here When your mother is not!  Put them out! Put them out!" Said the fish in the pot. "Have no fear, little fish," Said the Cat in the Hat.  "These Things are good Things." And he gave them a pat.  "They are tame. Oh, so tame! They have come here to play.  They will give you some fun On this wet, wet, wet day." "Now, here is a game that they like," Said the cat. "They like to fly kites," Said the Cat in the Hat. "No! Not in the house!" Said the fish in the pot.  "They should not fly kites In a house! They should not. Oh, the things they will bump! Oh, the things they will hit!  Oh, I do not like it! Not one little bit!" Then Sally and I Saw them run down the hall. We saw those two Things  Bump their kites on the wall! Bump! Thump! Thump! Bump! Down the wall in the hall. Thing Two and Thing One! They ran up! They ran down!  On the string of one kite We saw Mother's new gown!  Her gown with the dots That are pink, white and red.  Then we saw one kite bump On the head of her bed! Then those Things ran about With big bumps, jumps and kicks  And with hops and big thumps And all kinds of bad tricks. And I said, "I do NOT like the way that they play!  If Mother could see this, Oh, what would she say!" Then our fish said, “Look! LOOK!" And our fish shook with fear. "Your mother is on her way home! Do you hear? Oh, what will she do to us?  What will she say? Oh, she will not like it To find us this way!" "So, DO something! Fast!" said the fish.  "Do you hear! I saw her. Your mother! Your mother is near! So, as fast as you can,  Think of something to do!  You will have to get rid of Thing One and Thing Two!" So, as fast as I could, I went after my net. And I said, "With my net I can get them I bet.  I bet, with my net, I can get those Things yet!" And I said, "With my net I can get them I bet.  I bet, with my net, I can get those Things yet!" "Oh dear!" said the cat. "You did not like our game...  Oh dear. What a shame! What a shame!  What a shame!" Then he shut up the Things In the box with the hook.  And the cat went away With a sad kind of look. "That is good," said the fish. "He has gone away. Yes.  But your mother will come. She will find this big mess!  And this mess is so big And so deep and so tall,  We can not pick it up. There is no way at all!". Oh no! How would you clean up such a  big mess if it happened in your home? And THEN! Who was back in the house?  Why, the cat! "Have no fear of this mess," Said the Cat in the Hat. "I always pick up all my   playthings And so...  I will show you another Good trick that I know!" Then we saw him pick up All the things that were down. He picked up the cake,  And the rake, and the gown, And the milk, and the strings,  And the books, and the dish, And the fan, and the cup,  And the ship, and the fish. And he put them away.  Then he said, "That is that." And then he was gone With a tip of his hat. Then our mother came in And she said to us two,  "Did you have any fun? Tell me. What did you do?" And Sally and I did not know What to say.  Should we tell her The things that went on there that day? Should we tell her about it? Now, what SHOULD we do?  Well . . . What would you do  If your mother asked YOU? Lesson of the Story The story teaches us that while fun is important,  we must also be responsible and  make sure we clean up our messes  -just like the Cat in the Hat does at the end!" Fun Fact Dr. Seuss, whose real name was Theodor Seuss Geisel,  wrote The Cat in the Hat in 1957  to help children learn how to read.  He used just 236 different words to create this  fun and whimsical story that has become a classic!  Dr. Seuss was also known for his playful  rhymes and imaginative characters,  making his books favorites  for both kids and adults. Knowledge Check 1. What kind of day was it when the story began? a) Sunny and bright b) Snowy and cold  c) Rainy and wet d) Windy and cool The Answer is: c) Rainy and wet 2. Who were the two main children in the story? a) Jack and Jill b) Sally and her brother  c) Tom and Mary d) Max and Ruby The Answer is: b) Sally and her brother 3. What did the fish think  about the Cat in the Hat? a) The fish was excited and happy. b) The fish was curious and interested.  c) The fish was nervous and worried. d) The fish ignored the Cat. The Answer is: c) The fish  was nervous and worried. 4. What tricks did the Cat  do that made a big mess? a) Played with a ball of yarn. b) Juggled books, a fish,   and more while balancing on a ball. c) Danced around the house.  d) Baked a cake in the kitchen. The Answer is: b) Juggled books, a fish,  and more while balancing on a ball. 5. Who were Thing 1 and Thing  2, and what did they do? a) They were pets   that the Cat brought to play fetch. b) They were mischievous characters who   flew kites indoors and caused chaos. c) They were friendly robots   that cleaned up the house. d) They were clowns that performed funny tricks. The Answer is: b) They were mischievous characters  who flew kites indoors and caused chaos. 6. How did the children feel when  their mother was about to come home? a) Excited to show her what they did. b) Relaxed because the house was clean.  c) Nervous because the house was a mess. d) Happy because they had fun. The Answer is: c) Nervous  because the house was a mess. 7. What did the Cat do before he left the house? a) Made an even bigger mess. b) Ate all the food in the kitchen.  c) Cleaned up all the mess he made. d) Played more games with the children. The Answer is: c) Cleaned up all the mess he made. The End. 2. The Cat in The Hat Comes Back Our Featured Book Today is ... The Cat in the Hat Comes Back! By Dr. Seuss Creatively Read and Adapted by Lorenzo. Please Subscribe and Help my Channel Grow! Stay tuned for Fun Segments  at the End of the Story. The Cat in the Hat Comes Back! This was no time for play. This was no time for fun.  This was no time for games. There was work to be done. All that deep, Deep, deep snow,  All that snow had to go. When our mother went Down to the town for the day,  She said, "Somebody has to Clean all this away.  Somebody, SOMEBODY Has to, you see."  Then she picked out two Somebodies. Sally and me. Well. . . There we were.  We were working like that And then who should come up  But the CAT IN THE HAT! "Oh-oh!" Sally said. "Don't you talk to that cat.  That cat is a bad one, That Cat in the Hat.  He plays lots of bad tricks. Don't you let him come near.  You know what he did The last time he was here." Do you think Sally and her brother will have  fun now that the Cat in the Hat is back? "Play tricks?" laughed the cat. "Oh, my my! No, no, no!  I just want to go in To get out of the snow.  Keep your mind on your work. You just stay there, you two.  I will go in the house And find something to do." Then that cat went right in! He was up to no good!  So I ran in after As fast as I could! Do you know where I found him? You know where he was?  He was eating a cake in the tub! Yes he was! The hot water was on  And the cold water, too. And I said to the cat,  "What a bad thing to do!" "But I like to eat cake In a tub," laughed the cat.  "You should try it some time," Laughed the cat as he sat. And then I got mad. This was no time for fun.  I said, "Cat! You get out! There is work to be done.  I have no time for tricks. I must go back and dig.  I can't have you in here Eating cake like a pig!  You get out of this house! We don't want you about!"  Then I shut off the water And let it run out. The water ran out. And then I SAW THE RING!  A ring in the tub! And, oh boy! What a thing!  A big long pink cat ring! It looked like pink ink!  And I said, "Will this ever Come of? I don't think!" "Have no fear of that ring," Laughed the Cat in the Hat.  "Why, I can take cat rings Off tubs. Just like that!" Do you know how he did it? WITH MOTHER'S WHITE DRESS!  Now the tub was all clean, But her dress was a mess! Oh no! The Cat made a big mess!  Do you think he can clean it up? Then Sally looked in. Sally saw the dress, too!  And Sally and I Did not know what to do. We should work in the snow. But that dress! What a spot!  "It may never come off!" Sally said. "It may not!" But the cat laughed, "Ho! Ho!  I can make the spot go. The way I take spots off a dress Is just so!" "See here!" laughed the cat. "It is not hard at all.  The thing that takes spots Off a dress is a wall!" Then we saw the cat wipe The spot off the dress.  Now the dress was all clean. But the wall! What a mess! "Oh, wall spots!" he laughed. "Let me tell you some news.  To take spots off a wall, All I need is two shoes!" Whose shoes did he use? I looked and saw whose!  And I said to the cat, "This is very bad news.  Now the spot is all over DAD'S $10 SHOES!" "But your dad will not Know about that," Said the cat. "He will never find out," Laughed the Cat in the Hat.  "His $10 shoes will have No spots at all.  I will rub them right off On this rug in the hall." "But now we have rug spots!" I yelled. "What a day!  Rug spots! What next? Can you take THEM away?" "Don't ask me," he laughed. "Why, you know that I can!"  Then he picked up the rug And away the cat ran. "I can clean up these rug spots Before you count three!  No spots are too hard For a Hat Cat like me!" He ran into Dad's bedroom And then the cat said,  "It is good that your dad Has the right kind of bed." Then he shook the rug! CRACK! Now the bed had the spot! And all I could say was,  "Now what, Cat? NOW what?" But the cat just stood still. He just looked at the bed.  "This is NOT the right kind of a bed," The cat said. "To take spots off THIS bed Will be hard," said the cat.  "I can't do it alone," Said the Cat in the Hat. "It is good I have some one To help me," he said.  "Right here in my hat On the top of my head!  It is good that I have him Here with me today.  He helps me a lot. This is Little Cat A." And then Little Cat A Took the hat off HIS head. "It is good I have some one  To help ME," he said.  "This is Little Cat B. And I keep him about,  And when I need help Then I let him come out." And then B said, "I think we need Little Cat C. That spot is too much For the A cat and me.  But now, have no fear! We will clean it away! The three of us! Little Cats B, C and A!" "Come on! Take it away!" Yelled Little Cat A. "I will hit that old spot With this broom! Do you see?  It comes off the old bed! It goes on the T.V." And then Little Cat B Cleaned up the T.V. He cleaned it with milk, Put the spot in a pan!  And then C blew it out Of the house with a fan! "But look where it went!" I said. "Look where it blew! You blew the mess Out of the house. That is true.  But now you made Snow Spots! You can't let THEM stay!" "Let us think about that now," Said C, B and A. "With some help, we can do it!" Said Little Cat C.  Then POP! On his head We saw Little Cat D!  Then, POP! POP! Pop! Little Cats E, F and G! "We will clean up that snow If it takes us all day!  If it takes us all night, We will clean it away!"  Said Little Cats G, F, E, D, C, B, A. Wow! So many little cats! Will  they help or make a bigger mess? They ran out of the house then And we ran out, too.  And the Big Cat laughed, "Now you will see something new!  My cats are all clever. My cats are good shots.  My cats have good guns. They will kill all those spots!" But this did not look Very clever to me.  Kill snow spots with pop guns? That just could not be! "All this does is make MORE spots!" We yelled at the cat. "Your cats are no good.  Put them back in your hat. "Take your Little Cats G, F, E, D, C, B, A.  Put them back in your hat And you take them away!" "Oh, no!" said the cat. "All they need is more help.  Help is all that they need. So keep still and don't yelp." Then Little Cat G Took the hat off his head.  "I have Little Cat H Here to help us," he said. "Little Cats H, I, J, K, L and M.  But our work is so hard We must have more than them.  We need Little Cat N. We need O. We need P.  We need Little Cats Q, R, S, T, U and V." "Come on! Kill those spots! Kill the mess!" yelled the cats.  And they jumped at the snow With long rakes and red bats.  They put it in pails And they made high pink hills!  Pink snow men! Pink snow balls! And little pink pills! Oh, the things that they did! And they did them so hard,  It was all one big spot now All over the yard!  But the Big Cat stood there And he said, "This is good.  This is what they should do And I knew that they would. "With a little more help, All the work will be done. They need one more cat. And I know just the one." "Look close! In my hand I have Little Cat V.  On his head are Cats W, X, Y and Z." "What do you think is in Little Cat  Z's hat? Can it clean everything?" "Z is too small to see. So don't try. You can not.  But Z is the cat Who will clean up that spot!" "Now here is the Z You can't see," said the Cat.  "And I bet you can't guess What he has in HIS hat! "He has something called voOM. Voom is so hard to get,  You never saw anything Like it, I bet. Why, Voom cleans up anything  Clean as can be!" Then he yelled,  "Take your hat off now, Little Cat Z! Take the Voom of your head! Make it clean up the snow!  Hurry! You Little Cat! One! Two! Three! Go!" "So you see!" laughed the Cat, "Now your snow is all white!  Now your work is all done! Now your house is all right!  And you know where my little cats are?" Said the cat. "That Voom blew my little cats Back in my hat.  And so, if you ever Have spots, now and then,  I will be very happy To come here again . . . "... with Little Cats A, B, C, D...  E, F, G... H, I, J, K...  L, M, N... and O, P... . . . and Q, R, S, T... and Cat U and Cat V. . .  and Little Cats W X  Y and Z!" Lesson of the Story Sometimes things get harder  before they get better, but if you keep trying and use your imagination, you can solve even the biggest problems. Just like the Cat in the Hat, remember,  it's important to clean up your own mess! Fun Fact Did you know that Dr. Seuss wrote The Cat in the  Hat Comes Back as a sequel to The Cat in the Hat? In this book, Dr. Seuss uses the  alphabet, introducing Little Cats A to Z, to help children learn in a fun and creative way. It’s full of rhyming words and simple  language to make reading easier and more fun! Knowledge Check 1. What was the first mess the  Cat in the Hat made in the story?  A) He left dirty footprints on the floor B) He created a pink ring in the bathtub  C) He spilled cake all over the house D) He knocked over a vase  Answer: B) He created a pink ring in the bathtub 2. How did the Cat in the Hat try to clean the   pink ring in the tub? A) With soap and water  B) With a mop C) With mother's white dress  D) With a broom Answer: C) With mother's white dress 3. What finally cleaned up all the mess  in the snow at the end of the story?  A) Little Cat Z with "Voom"  B) The kids C) The mother  D) A big mop Answer: A) Little Cat Z with "Voom" The End 3. This is a book you READ ALOUD to find  out just how smart your tongue is.  The first time you read it, don't go fast!  This Fox is a tricky fox. He'll try to get your tongue in trouble. Take it SLOWLY. This Book is DANGEROUS! Fox in Socks Fox Socks Box Knox Knox in box. Fox in socks. Knox on fox in socks in box. Do you think you can keep up with Fox in Socks,  or will he twist your tongue in knots? Let's see how tricky this fox really is! Socks on Knox and Knox in box. Fox in socks on box on Knox. Chicks with bricks come. Chicks with blocks come.  Chicks with bricks and blocks and clocks come. Look, sir. Look, sir. You can make a quick trick chick stack.  You can make a quick trick clock stack. Ready to test how fast your tongue can  go, or will you need to take it slow? Do you choose to chew goo, too, sir?  If, sir, you, sir, choose to chew, sir,  with the Goo-Goose, chew, sir. Do, sir. Mr. Fox, sir, I won't do it.  I can't say it. I won't chew it. Very well, sir. Step this way.  We'll find another game to play. Do you think Fox is being too persistent when Mr.   Knox says he hates the game?  Let’s see what happens next! Bim comes. Ben comes.  Bim brings Ben broom. Ben brings Bim broom. Ben bends Bim's broom. Bim bends Ben's broom.  Bim's bends. Ben's bends. Ben's bent broom breaks. Bim's bent broom breaks. Ben's band. Luke's duck licks lakes. Duck takes licks in lakes Luke Luck likes.  Luke Luck takes licks in lakes duck likes. I can't blab such blibber blubber!  My tongue isn't made of rubber. Mr. Knox. Now come now. Come now.  You don't have to be so dumb now. . . . Try to say this, Mr. Knox, please . . . . Through three cheese trees three free fleas flew.  While these fleas flew, freezy breeze blew.  Freezy breeze made these three trees freeze.  Freezy trees made these trees' cheese freeze.  That's what made these three free fleas sneeze. Stop it! Stop it! That's enough, sir.  I can't say such silly stuff, sir. Very well, then, Mr. Knox, sir. Let's have a little talk about tweetle beetles. . . . How is your tongue doing? Are you having  fun reading all these tongue-twisting   words? Let’s see if your tongue is still  up for the last bit of this tricky story! What do you know about tweetle beetles?  Well... When tweetle beetles fight,  it's called a tweetle beetle battle. And when they battle in a puddle,  it's a tweetle beetle puddle battle. AND when tweetle beetles battle with paddles in a puddle,  they call it a tweetle beetle puddle paddle battle. AND . . . When beetles battle beetles in a puddle paddle battle  and the beetle battle puddle is a puddle in a bottle . . . they call this a tweetle beetle  bottle puddle paddle battle muddle.  AND . . . When beetles fight these battles  in a bottle with their paddles  and the bottle's on a poodle  and the poodle's eating noodles. . . . . . they call this a muddle puddle  tweetle poodle beetle noodle  bottle paddle battle. AND . . . Now wait a minute,  Mr. Socks Fox! When a fox is in the bottle where  the tweetle beetles battle with their paddles  in a puddle on a noodle-eating poodle,  THIS is what they call . . . . . . a tweetle beetle noodle poodle bottled  paddled muddled duddled  fuddled wuddled fox in socks, sir! Fox in socks, our game is done, sir.  Thank you for a lot of fun, sir. Now is your  Tongue Numb? Lesson of the Story: Fox in Socks teaches us that  sometimes things might be tricky,   but with patience and practice, we can  overcome even the toughest challenges. Whether it’s a tricky word or a tongue twister,   the key is to take it slowly  and have fun along the way! Fun Fact Fun Fact About Tongue Twisters: Did you know that tongue twisters like the ones in 'Fox in Socks' are used by  actors and public speakers  to improve their pronunciation and diction? Phrases like ‘Six sick bricks tick’ and  ‘Luke Luck likes lakes’ are not only fun to say but also help exercise the muscles in your mouth,   making your speech clearer. The next time you try to say  ‘tweetle beetle puddle paddle battle,’ remember, you're also giving your tongue a workout!
